# Forwood CRM Round Table 2026 – Vancouver Exploring the Future of Critical Risk Management

**Forwood’s 2026 CRM Round Table in Vancouver brought together senior safety, risk, and operational leaders from across our global customer community for a week of discussion focused on strengthening Critical Risk Management programs, sharing practical experiences, and exploring the future direction of CRM.**

The invitation-only event provides a unique opportunity for organisations to benchmark CRM maturity, share adoption learnings, and examine what drives meaningful and sustainable safety outcomes. Through peer-to-peer discussions and real-world experiences, participants explored both the challenges and opportunities facing Critical Risk Management programs today.

A major focus throughout the event was the industry’s continued shift from measuring activity to understanding assurance. Participants discussed how organisations can gain greater confidence that critical controls are not only being verified, but are effective, understood by the workforce, and delivering the intended risk reduction outcomes. Conversations highlighted the importance of verification quality, control effectiveness, leadership engagement, and meaningful evidence to support decision-making.

Another key area of interest was CRM maturity and benchmarking. Clients explored how maturity assessments can provide a more complete picture of program health, helping organisations identify improvement opportunities, support governance discussions, and understand how their programs compare against industry peers. The discussions reinforced a strong appetite for deeper insights that move beyond traditional usage metrics.

![](https://forwoodsafety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/IMG_7152-scaled.jpg)

Reporting and data analytics also featured prominently, with attendees sharing perspectives on how reporting can better support operational and executive decision-making. Rather than focusing solely on completion rates and activity levels, participants highlighted the value of identifying weak signals, emerging trends, and opportunities for targeted improvement.

The Round Table also provided an opportunity for clients to discuss the future of the Forwood platform through an early look at Forwood One. Conversations focused on the benefits of a more integrated and configurable platform, while also addressing important considerations such as mobile capability, offline functionality, reporting continuity, migration planning, and user adoption.

Additional sessions explored topics including action effectiveness reviews, AI and data insights, psychosocial risk management, multilingual usability, and practical approaches to CRM implementation and governance. A particular highlight was the sharing of real-world experiences from clients, providing valuable lessons on sustaining engagement, improving verification quality, and embedding Critical Risk Management into everyday operations.

Thank you to all participants for their openness, engagement, and willingness to share their experiences. The insights gathered throughout the week will continue to inform future product development, CRM maturity initiatives, benchmarking capabilities, and ongoing collaboration across the global CRM community.
